title: How the One Becomes the Many
reflection: Notice one label today that has hardened into a wall, such as a mood that became my whole life. Which working label could soften again?

o: Not mere illusion: the world is real but not what it first appears, and distinctions are not ultimate.
Pure illusion: the world is a dream, and a wise person simply stops taking any of it seriously.
A kind of magic: the world is made by tricks, and a clever person can see how they are done.
A kind of sin: the world is a trap, and a good person should turn away from it in disgust.
questions.e: Māyā is not illusion. The world is real; distinctions are real; but they are not ultimate. Difference is not separation.

questions.q: What picture does Conversation 1.5 use for many appearing from one?
o: One light and a prism: a single light shows as many colours, so difference is not separation.
One seed and a tree: the seed is used up, and only the tree is left to be seen afterwards.
One river and the sea: the river ends in the sea, and the two are no longer to be told apart.
One coin and its two sides: each side is quite separate, and the two can never be seen at once.
questions.e: The prism shows many colours from one light. The colours are real and different, but they are not separate from the light.

questions.q: “Telling food from poison, or your own child from another’s, is a useful kind of differentiation.”
questions.e: Differentiation is useful when it serves life. It binds only when a working label hardens into a wall, such as I am only this body, or a diagnosis that becomes who I am.
questions.c: Differentiation is useful until it hardens

questions.q: A man has been given a diagnosis and now says, “That is who I am.” Which point of Conversation 1.5 applies?
o: A working label has hardened into a wall: the diagnosis describes something, not all of him.
The label is wrong, so he should reject the diagnosis and refuse to talk about it again.
The label is the whole truth, so he should arrange his life around it from this day onward.
The label does not matter, so he should never mention it to those who are caring for him.
questions.e: A distinction that is useful becomes binding when it hardens: a mood becomes my whole life, a diagnosis becomes who I am. The lesson asks us to hold it as a working label.
questions.c: Hold a diagnosis as a working label, not as who you are

questions.q: A student says that space, time and causation must simply be an illusion. What does Conversation 1.5 say?
o: The scaffolding of a livable world: real, indispensable, conditioned, and relational.
An illusion, which a wise person sees through and then has no more use for at all.
Absolute, fixed and unchanging, as physics shows once it has described them fully.
Of no practical use, since everyday life is lived in the present moment alone.
questions.e: Without them there would be no livable world. But they are conditioned, and Einstein’s relativity shows them as relational, not absolute.
questions.c: Space, time and causation are the scaffolding

questions.q: A woman is troubled by a past that keeps coming back and a future that frightens her. What does Conversation 1.5 say about both?
o: The mind builds time: memory is rebuilt and the future simulated, both made now, so workable.
The past is fixed and the future is certain, so she should just prepare herself to accept both of them.
The past is gone and the future is unreal, so she should stop thinking about either one of them.
The past is real and the future is real, so she must try to fix the one and avoid the other.
questions.e: Memory is reconstruction and the future is simulation, both built in the present. This makes the haunting past and the frightening future workable, since they are constructions of this moment.
questions.c: The haunting past and frightening future are built now

questions.q: A man with low mood says that his past was always dark. What does Conversation 1.5 add?
o: Depression suffers a past rebuilt by low mood: memory is rebuilt, so the colouring is workable.
Depression gives the most accurate view of the past, so he should trust what he sees.
Depression has no effect on memory, so the past was dark exactly as he now remembers it.
Depression is caused by the past alone, so he should look for the first thing that went wrong.
questions.e: Depression suffers a past rebuilt by low mood, and anxiety a simulated future. Neither is fixed, which is why both are workable. This is gentle hope, not denial.
questions.c: Low mood rebuilds the past, so it is workable

questions.q: “Anxiety suffers a simulated future, and because the simulation is made by the mind, it can be worked with.”
questions.e: The future is simulation, built from memory and mood. Seeing this does not deny that the fear is real; it shows that the fear is made, and so can be remade.
questions.c: Anxiety is a simulated future, and workable

questions.q: A teacher wants to try the experiment of Conversation 1.5 today. What does it ask?
o: Find one label that has hardened into a wall, and ask whether it could soften into a working label.
Drop every label for the day, so as to see the world as it is, with no names for anything.
Add as many labels as she can, so as to see the world as it is, in the greatest detail.
Ask others which label fits her best, and then keep that label for the rest of her life.
questions.e: The experiment is gentle: notice one label that has hardened, such as a mood that became my whole life, and ask whether it could be held as working.

questions.q: What do ground and flow have in common, in Conversation 1.5?
o: Brahman and Śakti, Prakāśa and Vimarśa, stillness and movement: one architecture.
Three unrelated ideas, taken from three different schools of thought, which merely sound alike.
Three stages, in which a person leaves the ground behind in order to join the flow of things.
Three rivals, whose claims a person must weigh up before choosing the one that fits best.
questions.e: The lesson ties Module 1 together: the ground and the flow are not two. Brahman and Śakti, Prakāśa and Vimarśa, stillness and movement describe one architecture.
questions.c: Ground and flow are one architecture
